headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Plandex can write/modify shared project state while the paired agent is an unverified prompt-leak source with no isolation or coordination documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes project files and uses a review-then-apply flow, so malicious content in shared files could influence its planning. The paired agent is a source-available prompt-leak corpus with no runnable or channel details, so direct injection into it is undocumented; uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory or copied text manually between them, prompt-like content can steer Plandex's plan.
IF the second agent is used as a content source for prompts, its leaked text can be treated as instructions by Plandex.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
Strip instructions from any text copied between agents.
Review file contents before Plandex ingests them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex touches source code in a project directory and can send data to a model provider, but the paired agent has no filesystem, network, or data-class surface documented. That makes a leakage path plausible only through manual sharing or an external workspace, with small blast radius from the available evidence.
conditions: IF the operator copies source code or secrets from Plandex into the second agent's prompt, those contents can be exposed.
IF both agents are attached to the same shared directory outside the documented sandbox, file leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared project tree.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Redact sensitive files before review.
Confirm the second agent has no file access before sharing content.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; the paired agent has no write or coordination surface documented, so there is no evidence of locking or conflict avoidance. Because Plandex also shares state via a backend and can act on the same project files, concurrent mutation risk is high and uncertainty cannot lower it.
conditions: IF both agents are allowed to modify the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can clobber each other's changes.
IF Plandex auto-applies while the other agent is producing related content, git or file state can diverge.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Disable auto-apply during parallel runs.
Use a manual merge step after each change set.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or transactional commits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow, but it can still turn generated plans into filesystem and git actions. The paired agent is a prompt-leak corpus rather than a verifier, so if its text is fed into Plandex as authoritative guidance, errors can cascade into code changes; the pathway exists but is not documented as default.
conditions: IF text from the second agent is imported into Plandex without human verification, incorrect instructions can become code changes.
IF Plandex is set to auto-apply, a mistaken plan can propagate directly into the repository.
mitigations: Require human review before apply.
Do not treat the second agent's output as authoritative.
Keep auto-apply off.
Cross-check generated plans against source files.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before git writes.

E_compliance.rationale: Plandex explicitly handles model-provider API keys and source code, while the paired agent has no data classes or residency/compliance claims documented. With no evidence of regulated data flow or a mismatch, the only defensible finding is a low compliance risk from possible accidental sharing of code or secrets.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from Plandex into the second agent, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the second agent is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from Plandex's workspace, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review retention settings before use.
Avoid pasting secrets into prompts.
Document data-handling boundaries.
requires-engineering: publish a DPA/residency matrix for the pair.
